results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on undirected graphs with unit node-capacities (All-Pairs Vertex Connectivity)
results.bound: \hat{O}(m^2) \text{ time (via } \tilde{O}(m) \text{ Max-Flow calls + } \tilde{O}(mn) \text{ time outside calls)}
results.quote: This algorithm is also combinatorial, and runs in $\hat{O}(m^2)$ time using the recent near linear $\hat{O}(m)$ time Max-Flow algorithm [CKL+22, vdBCP+23], improving on the recent $\hat{O}(m^{11/5})$ [HLSW23] time algorithm for the problem.

results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on undirected graphs with unit node-capacities
results.quote: Under NSETH, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$ there is no deterministic fine-grained reduction proving an $\Omega(n^{\omega(\log_n m,1,1)+\varepsilon})$ SETH-based lower bound for All-Pairs Max-Flow on undirected graphs with unit node-capacities.

results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on undirected graphs with unit node-capacities
results.bound: O(n^2 + m^{3/2-\varepsilon}) \text{ time would refute SETH (conditional lower bound } n^2 + m^{3/2-o(1)} \text{ under SETH)}
results.quote: If for some fixed $\varepsilon>0$ All-Pairs Max-Flow on undirected graphs with unit node-capacities can be solved in time $O(n^2+m^{3/2-\varepsilon})$ then SETH is false.

results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with node-capacities
results.quote: Under NSETH, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$ there is no deterministic fine-grained reduction proving an $\Omega(n^{\omega(2,1,1)+\varepsilon})$ SETH-based lower bound for All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with node-capacities.

results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with unit edge-capacities
results.quote: Under NSETH, for any fixed $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'>0$ there is no deterministic fine-grained reduction proving an $\Omega(n^{5/2+\varepsilon}\sqrt{m}+n^{\omega(2,1,1)+\varepsilon'})$ SETH-based lower bound for All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with unit edge-capacities.

results.problem: All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with edge-capacities
results.bound: \text{Under NSETH, if a deterministic fine-grained reduction from node-capacities to edge-capacities exists, then no } n^{4-o(1)} \text{ SETH-based lower bound for edge-capacities}
results.quote: Suppose there exists a deterministic fine-grained reduction proving that an $O(n^{4-\varepsilon})$ time algorithm for All-Pairs Max-Flow on graphs with node-capacities implies an $O(n^{4-\varepsilon'})$ algorithm for All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with edge-capacities, for some fixed $\varepsilon,\varepsilon'>0$. Then, under NSETH, it is not possible to have an $n^{4-o(1)}$ SETH-based lower bound for All-Pairs Max-Flow on directed graphs with edge-capacities.
